title: KB Securities and Suho Iocean Complete Tokenized Bond Lifecycle Pilot
description: KB Securities and Suho Iocean tested simulated tokenized bonds using ERC-3643, atomic delivery-versus-payment settlement and automated ledger reconciliation exceeding 99.9%.
why_it_matters: The pilot demonstrates how a Korean brokerage could connect tokenized securities to existing bond records, settlement controls and maturity processing. It is a technical rehearsal ahead of planned legal changes, not evidence of a live retail investment product.
keyTakeaways: The November 17 announcement concerns a completed technical pilot, not a commercial tokenized-bond launch.
ERC-3643 was used to create simulated bond tokens linked to brokerage records through an API.
Delivery-versus-payment logic and automated ledger checks reportedly achieved over 99.9% reconciliation.
The trial included automated maturity redemption and token burning; stablecoin links remain prospective.
body:
South Korea's KB Securities and blockchain infrastructure provider Suho Iocean have completed a pilot covering the lifecycle of simulated tokenized bonds, from issuance and settlement through maturity redemption. The companies reported the exercise on November 17, 2026, according to separate accounts from Yonhap and Newsis.

The project was conducted under a 2026 blockchain application programming interface development program supported by the Ministry of Science and ICT and the Korea Internet and Security Agency. KB Securities supplied the brokerage use case while Suho Iocean provided the technical infrastructure.

Using the compliance-oriented ERC-3643 standard, the pilot linked KB Securities' bond data to simulated blockchain securities. Its delivery-versus-payment design paired securities transfers with payment so that failure of either side would reverse the transaction. Automated checks between the blockchain and the brokerage's internal records reportedly produced a matching rate above 99.9%. The test also automated maturity payments and token destruction.

Newsis reported a simulated small-ticket investment flow using KB reward points. The participants described possible future stablecoin integration, contingent on legislation. No public commercial launch or live stablecoin settlement was announced.

facts.claim: KB Securities and Suho Iocean reported completing a simulated tokenized bond lifecycle pilot on November 17.
The pilot was part of a 2026 government-supported blockchain API development program involving KISA.
The pilot applied ERC-3643 and delivery-versus-payment settlement that reverses a transaction if either leg fails.
Automatic reconciliation between blockchain and brokerage ledgers reportedly achieved a match rate exceeding 99.9 percent.
The simulated bond investment process used KB reward points for small-ticket participation and automated maturity redemption.
